articles.full_text:
यूपी: अगस्त और सितंबर में जुलाई से भी कम हो सकती है प्रदेश में बारिश, बढ़ सकता है अधिकतम और न्यूनतम तापमान
Weather in UP: मौसम विभाग ने यूपी के मौसम को लेकर एक डराने वाली चेतावनी जारी की है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार अगस्त और सितंबर में जुलाई से भी कम बारिश हो सकती है।
खबरें लगातार पढ़ने के लिए अमर उजाला एप डाउनलोड करें
या
वेबसाइट पर पढ़ना जारी रखने के लिए वीडियो विज्ञापन देखें
अगर आपके पास प्रीमियम मेंबरशिप है तो
विस्तार
भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (आईएमडी) ने दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून के दूसरे चरण (अगस्त-सितंबर) के लिए वर्षा और तापमान का पूर्वानुमान जारी किया है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार,अगस्त और सितंबर के दौरान प्रदेश सहित देश भर में सामान्य से कम बारिश का आसार है।
वर्षा दीर्घकालिक औसत के 94 प्रतिशत से कम रहने की संभावना है। इसकी वजह से अधिकांश हिस्सों में बारिश कम हो सकती है। हालांकि, उत्तरी हिस्सों और पूर्वी व पूर्वोत्तर के कुछ हिस्सों में सामान्य या सामान्य से अधिक बारिश की उम्मीद है। अगस्त महीने के दौरान भी कुल बारिश सामान्य से कम रहने का अनुमान है।
पूर्वोत्तर के सीमित इलाकों को छोड़कर ज्यादातर जगहों पर बारिश की कमी महसूस की जा सकती है। इसकी वजह से अधिकांश हिस्सों में अगस्त के दौरान मासिक औसत अधिकतम तापमान सामान्य से अधिक रहेगा। केवल उत्तर-पश्चिम व मध्य के कुछ हिस्सों और उससे सटे प्रायद्वीपीय क्षेत्रों में यह सामान्य या उससे कम हो सकता है। देश के ज्यादातर हिस्सों में रात का औसत तापमान (न्यूनतम तापमान) सामान्य या सामान्य से अधिक रहने का अनुमान है।
आज शाम तक इन क्षेत्रों में हो सकती है बारिश
उत्तर प्रदेश के पूर्वांचल क्षेत्र के जिलों में आज बारिश हो सकती है, जबकि मध्य और अवध के क्षेत्रों में आसमान में बादल छाए हैं। मौसम विभाग द्वारा जारी बुलेटिन के अनुसार, राज्य के एक बड़े हिस्से में हल्की से मध्यम बारिश, आकाशीय बिजली चमकने और 30 से 40 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चल रही हैं। विभाग ने विशेष रूप से सोनभद्र, आजमगढ़, मऊ तथा इनके आसपास के इलाकों के लिए चेतावनी जारी की है। वहीं कुछ अन्य जिलों में भी हल्की से मध्यम वर्षा के साथ आकाशीय बिजली गिरने और तेज हवाएं चलने का अनुमान व्यक्त किया गया है।
इन जिलों में बादल छाए रहने की संभावना
पूर्वांचल व मध्य यूपी से जुड़े सोनभद्र, मिर्जापुर, प्रयागराज, संत रविदास नगर, जौनपुर, बलिया, प्रतापगढ़, सुल्तानपुर, अंबेडकर नगर, देवरिया, अयोध्या और गोरखपुर में बारिश की संभावना है। वहीं पश्चिमी यूपी व तराई क्षेत्रों जैसे इटावा, आगरा, फिरोजाबाद, मैनपुरी, एटा, हाथरस, मथुरा, कासगंज, कन्नौज, फर्रुखाबाद, बहराइच, गोंडा, सिद्धार्थ नगर, बलरामपुर, श्रावस्ती, शाहजहांपुर, लखीमपुर खीरी, बरेली, पीलीभीत और अलीगढ़ में बादल छाए रहने की संभावना जताई गई है।

articles.title: Air-conditioned dress shirts arrive in Japan to save working professionals from sweltering heat - SoraNews24

articles.full_text:
These dress shirts are sure to have fans.
If you need business attire in Japan, Yofuku no Aoyama is pretty much always a safe choice. They may not have the trendiest fashions from brand-name designers, but they can set you up with outfits appropriately dressy for a day in the office or a meeting with clients, and at affordable prices too.
For example, here’s one of their new button-up shirts. Nothing flashy or overly fancy, but a respectable, understated summer business look.
Now, looking at that photo, you might get the impression that the person wearing it is a little on the stocky side. However, the puffiness of the shirt isn’t a result of overindulgence in edible fireworks sweets, taco sweets, or convenience store-flavor fried chicken. It’s actually because this isn’t just a dress shirt, it’s also a wearable cooling system, and its fans are engaged in the image above.
Look closely, and you’ll see that there’s actually a fan positioned inside the shirt, near the small of the back. Actually, there are two fans, one on each side, and when switched on they provide blasts of cool air, directed inwards to cool down the wearer and help them deal with the summer heat.
Air-conditioned garments like this have become more popular in Japan in recent years, but mainly as an extension of equipment for workers in fields such as construction, garbage disposal, and event crowd control. As such, they’ve usually looked like blue-collar uniform vests or jackets, more “gear” than “apparel.” But with summers in Japan getting hotter and hotter, more and more people have been showing an interest in cooled garments, and Yofuku no Aoyama has responded with its new shirts, developed in partnership with fan-equipped fashion maker FZN to create an option for business settings.
Though the fan is noticeable from behind, the designers have done a pretty impressive job concealing it from other angles.
Yofuku no Aoyama says extensive efforts were made to keep the system’s weight down to keep the shirt comfortable to wear, with the two fans weighing 95 grams (3.4 ounces) each and the rechargeable battery pack 165 grams.
Yofuku no Aoyama doesn’t make any mention, though, of how loud the fans are, though, which would suggest that they’re not necessarily whisper-quiet. However, the point of the Kucho Wear Short-sleeved Shirt (as the item is called), isn’t necessarily to run it during meetings with colleagues of clients, as those conversations will be taking place inside air-conditioned conference rooms. Instead, the appeal of an air-conditioned dress shirt is that you can run the fans while you’re running around the city, heading from one meeting to another while being exposed to the elements, and won’t need to change into more formal clothing once you arrive at your destination.
The “entry complete set,” which includes the shirt (available in blue or gray and sizes medium, large, or extra-large) plus the fans, battery pack, and charging cable, is priced at 17,490 yen (US$107) is on sale now at Yofuku no Ayoama stores and through the company’s online shop here.
Source: PR Times

articles.title: Japan expects extreme heat to persist - nhk.or.jp

articles.full_text:
Scorching weather has gripped wide areas of Japan, with the mercury climbing to near 40 degrees Celsius in the Tokai and Kyushu regions. The extreme heat is expected to continue on Sunday, including in quake-hit Kumamoto Prefecture.
The Japan Meteorological Agency said a high pressure system continued to cover wide areas from eastern to western Japan on Saturday, pushing up temperatures.
A high of 39.7 degrees was marked in Hamamatsu City, Shizuoka Prefecture and 39.5 degrees in Misato Town, Miyazaki Prefecture. The daytime high in central Tokyo was 36.5 degrees.
Highs in Kumamoto Prefecture, where a powerful earthquake caused extensive damage, reached 37.5 degrees in Kosamachi, 36.6 degrees in Kumamoto City and 35.9 degrees in Yatsushiro City.
Nighttime temperatures are expected to remain above 25 degrees in many parts, including in quake-hit Kumamoto.
Weather officials are forecasting even higher temperatures on Sunday, reaching 40 degrees in Hita City, Oita Prefecture. A high of 39 degrees is expected in the cities of Nagoya, Gifu, Yamaguchi, Saga and Miyakonojo. And a high of 38 degrees is projected for the cities of Osaka, Okayama, Takamatsu and Kagoshima. A high of 35 degrees is expected in central Tokyo.
The outlook for Kumamoto Prefecture on Sunday includes highs of 38 degrees in Hitoyoshi City and 37 degrees in Kumamoto City. Weather officials say the temperature in Kumamoto City could hit 40 degrees on Monday.
People cleaning up after the earthquake and those engaged in recovery efforts are advised to avoid work in the hottest hours, replenish water and salt frequently and take enough rest.
Heatstroke alerts have been issued for 30 of the country's 47 prefectures from the Kanto region in the east to the Kyushu and Okinawa in the southwest.
In northeastern Japan, developed rainclouds are in the Tohoku region as warm, humid air is flowing into a low pressure system and rain front. A Level 4 Urgent Warning for landslides has been issued for parts of Iwate, Yamagata and Miyagi prefectures.
The front and low pressure system are expected to pass over the Tohoku region on Sunday. Weather officials say atmospheric conditions will become unstable not only in the Tohoku region but also in the Kanto-Koshin region. These regions can expect heavy rain accompanied by thunder.
Officials are urging extreme caution against landslides in the Tohoku region. People are also advised to stay on alert for flooding in low-lying areas, swollen rivers, lightning and gusty winds.

articles.title: IMD issues red alert for 8 Kerala districts as heavy rains trigger landslides, floods; 6 killed - The Times of India
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Heavy rains lashed several parts of Kerala on Saturday, triggering landslides, flooding low-lying areas, swelling rivers and dams, and prompting authorities to launch large-scale rescue and evacuation operations in affected regions.
According to a statement from the Chief Minister's Office (CMO), six people were killed in rain-related incidents across the state.
Four of the deaths occurred in separate landslides in Idukki and Kottayam districts, where several others were rescued, the statement added.
Search operations for the six missing people continued with teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Fire and Rescue Services, police, the Coast Guard, local administration officials, public representatives and residents taking part in the efforts, the statement said.
It added that 65 relief camps had been set up across the state, providing shelter to 1,465 people affected by the rains.
According to news agency PTI, CM V D Satheesan said 17 houses were completely destroyed, while another 127 suffered partial damage in rain-related incidents.
Two separate fatal landslides were reported in Idukki district.
The deceased was identified as 65-year-old Sumathi, a resident of Adoormala near Kudayathoor.
Her husband Ravi and son Ratheesh were rescued and admitted to a hospital, officials said.
In another incident, Prabhakaran Nair (77) of Vaikom died after a landslide hit the house of his relative in the Vagamon area of Idukki district.
A youth died, and his mother was trapped under debris after a landslide at Payyanithottam in Poonjar in Kottayam district.
The deceased was identified as Josephine, son of Johny. His mother, Rejina Johny (46), was trapped under debris, officials said.
Following the landslides and flooding, Satheesan directed ministers in charge of rain-hit districts to stay in their respective districts and oversee rescue and relief operations as heavy rains continued across the state.
He reviewed the situation with ministers and district collectors.
Landslides and flooding hit several parts of Idukki district.
At Upputhara, a parked police jeep was damaged after a landslide, while heavy rains disrupted traffic at several locations.
Vehicular movement on the Kochi-Dhanushkodi National Highway was affected following a landslide near Cheeyapara.
Rising water levels in the Chottupara stream at Vandiperiyar caused waterlogging on National Highway 183, affecting traffic movement.
In neighbouring Kottayam district, heavy rain triggered widespread flooding in Erattupetta, Kanjirappally, Koottickal, Erumeli and Pala, inundating commercial and residential areas, disrupting traffic and prompting rescue operations.
Four houses were damaged in a landslide at Teekoy village, but residents escaped unhurt, officials said.
Around 2,500 chickens died after floodwaters entered a poultry farm at Pala in Kottayam.
The poultry farm, owned by Jineesh Alex of Mulaykkal House, has been operating for the past 18 years.
More landslides were reported from the hilly areas of Pathanamthitta district.
Ranni MLA Pazhakulam Madhu, in a social media post, said heavy flooding had been reported in Ranni and adjoining areas.
As floodwaters entered shops and houses, several residents were shifted to relief camps.
Several areas in Ranni, Kozhencherry and Aranmula, located along the banks of the Pampa river, were cut off due to flooding.
The district administration deployed boats to rescue people stranded in their homes, officials said.
Besides the central Kerala districts, floods and minor landslides were reported in Ernakulam, Thrissur, Kozhikode, Malappuram, Kannur, Kasaragod and Palakkad districts.
Engapuzha town in Kozhikode was completely inundated after river water entered the area following heavy rainfall.
Landslides were reported from several high-range areas of Kozhikode and Kannur districts, officials said.
Traffic on ghat roads in Wayanad and Idukki was regulated following minor landslides in those areas.
Kerala Revenue Minister A P Anilkumar said the government was fully prepared to deal with landslides, flooding and other rain-related emergencies.
"We have already opened relief camps wherever required. Even if the intensity of the rain decreases, people living in high-risk areas will be shifted to camps as a precautionary measure," he said.
Shutters of dams in Thiruvananthapuram, Pathanamthitta, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur and Kannur districts were opened following rising water levels.
The shutters of the Thottappally spillway and barrages in Alappuzha district were also opened to prevent flooding.
Sea incursion affected coastal areas of Ernakulam, Alappuzha, Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod districts, officials said.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a 'red alert' for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts, forecasting extremely heavy rainfall.
An 'orange alert' was issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur and Palakkad districts.
Kerala State Disaster Management Authority member secretary Sekhar Lukose Kuriakos said exceptionally heavy rainfall in central Kerala had triggered landslides, mudslides and flooding in several districts.
A 'red alert' denotes extremely heavy rainfall of over 204 mm in 24 hours, while an 'orange alert' indicates very heavy rainfall ranging between 115 mm and 204 mm.
(With agency inputs)

articles.title: Gujarat Rain Fury: Four Dead, 16,500 Evacuated As IMD Issues Red Alert - vibesofindia.com
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
Relentless rainfall continued to batter several parts of Gujarat on Friday, claiming four lives, forcing thousands of people to move to safer places, and putting the entire state administration on high alert. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for five districts and an orange alert for 11 others, warning of more heavy rainfall on Saturday.
With rivers overflowing, roads submerged and rescue teams deployed across vulnerable areas, the state government has appealed to people to stay indoors and avoid unnecessary travel.
Three Farm Labourers Die of Electrocution in Navsari
One of the most tragic incidents was reported from Gandevi taluka in Navsari district, where three farm labourers lost their lives after the tempo truck they were travelling in came into contact with a live high-tension overhead power line.
According to police, the accident occurred on Friday morning while the labourers were travelling from Gandeva village to a nearby farm. Heavy rainfall and poor visibility are believed to have contributed to the incident. The deceased have been identified as:
Kalpesh Halpati (30)
Nitin Halpati (32)
Jigar Halpati (21)
All three were residents of Gandeva village.
Two other labourers suffered serious injuries in the accident and were shifted to a hospital in Kharel for treatment.
Gandevi Police Inspector N.I. Rathod said continuous rainfall and low visibility likely played a major role in the accident.
11-Year-Old Girl Swept Away in Anand
In another heartbreaking incident, an 11-year-old girl died after being swept away by strong water currents in a canal in Borsad taluka of Anand district.
The incident happened on Friday as the girl was near the canal along with her siblings. While the other children were rescued safely, the young girl was swept away and lost her life.
Rainfall Crosses 61% of Seasonal Average
According to a state government release, Gujarat has already received 61.5 per cent of its seasonal rainfall by Friday evening.
The continuous showers have caused flooding in several districts, waterlogging in low-lying areas and rising water levels in rivers and canals, prompting large-scale rescue and evacuation efforts.
More Than 16,500 People Shifted to Safer Places
As a precaution, authorities evacuated more than 16,500 people from flood-prone areas across Gujarat. In addition, 41 people were rescued from different locations where they had become trapped due to rising water levels.
Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel personally reviewed the flood situation during a late-night visit to the State Emergency Operations Centre (SEOC). Officials briefed him on rescue operations, weather forecasts and preparedness measures being taken across the state.
Army, Air Force and Disaster Teams Ready
To deal with any emergency, multiple agencies have been deployed across Gujarat. Two Army columns each have been stationed in:
Ahmedabad
Navsari
Surat
Meanwhile, Air Force helicopters have been kept on standby at:
Jamnagar
Jodhpur
Vadodara
Pune
These helicopters will be used for rescue and relief operations if the weather situation worsens. The state has also deployed:
33 teams of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)
17 teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)
These teams have been positioned in vulnerable districts to respond quickly to flooding, rescue operations and other emergencies.
Gandevi Remains Worst-Hit Area
Navsari’s Gandevi taluka continues to be one of the worst-affected regions after days of heavy rainfall. District authorities have closed 11 panchayat roads as they remain unsafe for travel. People living in flood-prone villages, including:
Torangam
Devdha
Undach
Khakhwada
Ajrai
have been shifted to relief shelters.
Officials said priority is being given to evacuating elderly citizens, pregnant women, children, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable residents.
Government Urges People to Stay Indoors
State Relief Commissioner Gaurang Makwana has appealed to residents not to leave their homes unless it is a medical emergency. He advised people to:
Avoid unnecessary travel.
Stay away from rivers, canals and overflowing water bodies.
Keep away from waterlogged roads and low-lying areas.
Follow official weather updates and administration advisories.
Authorities have warned that the situation could worsen if heavy rainfall continues over the next two days.
Ahmedabad Tightens Safety Measures
Following the IMD’s heavy rain forecast till August 2, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) has stepped up safety measures across the city. Entry to all lakefront gardens has been banned on Friday and Saturday as a precaution.
The AMC has also postponed Friday’s celebrations marking the conclusion of the annual Gauri and Jaya-Parvati fast, which were scheduled to be held at the Sabarmati Riverfront and Kankaria Lakefront.
Municipal Commissioner Banchhanidhi Pani urged residents to remain indoors unless absolutely necessary and asked citizens to stay alert during the ongoing spell of heavy rain.
Fire Department on 24-Hour Alert
The Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services Department has significantly increased its preparedness to respond to any emergency caused by heavy rainfall. Key arrangements include:
All 19 fire stations operating at full capacity.
678 fire and rescue personnel deployed on 24-hour standby.
Holidays of all officers and staff cancelled to ensure adequate manpower.
Continuous monitoring from the AMC’s Monsoon Control Room.
Officials said every possible step has been taken to ensure immediate emergency response across the city.
Rescue Boats Ready for Flood Emergencies
The AMC has also kept eight rescue boats on standby for flood rescue operations. Each boat has a trained crew of seven members, who will remain on duty round the clock to respond immediately if flooding occurs.
Dedicated teams of officers and emergency staff will continue to monitor rainfall and weather conditions from the city’s main monsoon control room throughout the day.
Red Alert Continues as State Remains on High Alert
With more heavy rainfall expected over the weekend, Gujarat remains on high alert. Rescue agencies, the Army, Air Force, SDRF, NDRF and local authorities are working together to respond to emergencies and protect residents in vulnerable areas.
Officials have once again urged people to avoid unnecessary travel, stay away from flooded roads and water bodies, and follow official advisories until weather conditions improve.

articles.title: Sivasagar Flash Flood: DC Cites No IMD Warning, Rapid Surge - Prag News
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
Sivasagar district faced an unprecedented disaster on July 19, with authorities having a mere three hours to respond before flash floodwaters from Nagaland's hills overwhelmed local rivers, according to District Commissioner Mridul Yadav. The rapid onset, described as a “flash flood,” unfolded too quickly for conventional disaster protocols, exacerbating one of the worst deluges in the district's history.
Mr. Yadav revealed that the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had issued no warning regarding extremely heavy rainfall that could have indicated the impending scale of the disaster. The gravity of the situation became apparent to the Sivasagar administration around 12:30 pm on July 19, when a crucial call came from the Deputy Commissioner of Mokokchung in Nagaland.
The Mokokchung official reportedly sought immediate assistance with boats for rescue operations, informing Sivasagar authorities that several villages on the Nagaland side were already submerged due to the rapidly rising levels of the Jhanji River. This sudden inundation on the upstream side left Sivasagar with extremely limited time to prepare or mobilize effective pre-emptive measures, leading to rescue teams being cut off as waters surged.
The incident underscores the critical challenges posed by sudden, unpredicted natural calamities originating from upstream regions, particularly when traditional warning systems fail to provide adequate lead time for response.
